propositions: Plans delivering infrastructure via automated pipelines or environment/infrastructure applies must prove runtime-only correctness risks (boot, auth, connect, readiness) through the fastest out-of-loop experiment (local/emulated or manual probe against real target) before committing mechanisms into slow delivery loops.

The plan-review criterion T15 overlay applies when a mechanism is codified in an automated pipeline, one pass is slow/costly (minutes-to-hours), and correctness depends only on runtime behavior in a realistic environment.

For each named runtime risk, the plan must commit to a concrete, fast (minutes-scale) experiment outside the slow loop that returns a verdict, completed before the mechanism is codified—not a vague post-deploy verification.

Transient de-risk experiments and their cleanup must remove only artifacts the experiment created, never touching pre-existing or shared resources, to avoid scope creep into persistent infrastructure.
T10's production-hardening rubric must be partitioned to exclude transient throwaway experiments used for de-risking, scoping T10 to durable infrastructure only.
